editorial:
Every morning, Christine wakes up with no memory of who she is or what happened to her. Her husband Ben patiently explains her past, but when a doctor secretly gives her a camera to record daily video diaries, she starts uncovering pieces of a story that do not match what she has been told. The movie pulls you into her confusion and fear, making you question every person around her. Nicole Kidman carries the film with a raw, emotional performance, and the tight, quiet setting keeps the tension high without needing big action scenes.

The pacing is steady and suspenseful, with twists that keep you guessing until the end. Colin Firth and Mark Strong add strong support, though some plot turns feel a bit too convenient. If you enjoy psychological thrillers that mess with your head, this one is worth your time. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Christine learns that Ben is not really her husband. The man calling himself Ben is actually the attacker who caused her memory loss, and he has been lying to her for years. The real Ben is someone else entirely. Christine's video diary and the doctor's help expose the truth. In the end, the fake Ben is stopped, and Christine finally begins to rebuild her life with her real family, holding onto hope that her memories may slowly return.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers with twists.
